ZS - CAR

By: Joy Summers | Paid

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
A legal battle has broken out between the Director of our civil aviation authority Poppy Khoza and her former head of the accident and incident investigation division Peter Mashaba. Does an accident i

Unique Selling Point:
AN EXCLUSIVE INTERVIEW WITH PETER MASHABA - former executive responsible for the Accident and Incident investigation division at the CAA

Summary:
Khoza says he breached CAA confidentiality, insulted and defamed her. He says that she was warned that the CAA’s own plane would crash – she ignored the warnings and indeed a month later the CAA citation jet crashed in George and killed all three of its own crew.

Khoza never renewed Mashaba’s contract and wanted an apology from him. He refused.
The CAA and Khoza then went to court to gag Mashaba from any further utterances. Incredibly although this was about airline safety in South Africa and it called into question the regulatory authority’s own safety protocols, the matter was heard in camera. Carte Blanche tried to gain access to the courts and wrote a letter to the judge but we were rebuffed. The end result was that an interim interdict gagged Mashaba from speaking out and the CAA continued and Mashaba struggled on.

But as with any investigation an independent body must do an accident investigation and make the final report public. In this case it was the Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau (AAIB) of Ethiopian Airlines. Tomorrow the report will be released by the DOT. And its findings says Mashaba vindicate what he was saying all along. Now he is fighting for his job back.



Further information:
The findings suggest numerous breaches of safety by the CAA itself. And the allegations of an attempted cover up by the CAA is doing the rounds on pilot and aviation groups.
Carte Blanche speaks to the main role players and investigates if the CAA tried to cover up, and put pressure on the Ethiopian Bureau to change the findings.



Extra Budget Items:
We have no visuals so we will need extra budget for graphics.

Script:


ZS CAR – A DOOMED FLIGHT FINAL SCRIPT FOR TX Sunday 30th January 2022

Commentary One
23rd January 2020. George Airport.

At 8 35 am three flight crew from the Civil Aviation Authority, waited for clearance for take- off on runway 1.1

Music up sound

Captain Thabiso Tolo, first officer Tebogo Lekalakala and flight inspector Gugu Mnguni were assigned to a division called the Flight inspection unit and were on board this plane owned by the CAA.

Their function was to calibrate or fine tune instrument landing systems at airports across South Africa so aviation traffic can be guided to safety in poor visibility. The CAA are paid for this service

Commentary Two
Before take-off Lekalakala spoke to her husband, Jacob

Jacob
She called me, said look, I can't talk for long because we're going out again, you know, we're just refuelling. I just wanted to tell you, I love you and then we'll all talk when we land.

Commentary Three
But Jacob would never again hear his wife’s voice

Jacob
That was supposed to be the first day in George. And that was the last call.

Commentary Four
What led to the accident that claimed her life and that of her colleagues remains shrouded in mystery. The planes final moments providing only clues.

At 8 42 am the Cessna Citation was airborne, climbing to 3000 feet. Eight minutes later it began a right turn, appearing to level off at 4000 feet before climbing again

But a few minutes later the flight data recorder shows that something was horribly wrong –
The plane was both pitching and rolling. At 105 degrees it was almost inverted with its nose down.

Then it returned to 75 degrees but seconds later it lost 1500 feet in 9 seconds and disappeared off the radar at 8 52 am.
The wreckage discovered, strewn across the top of an Outeniqua mountain.


Commentary five
Captain Tolo’s wife, Simnikiwe, recalls the moment she was given the news

Simnikiwe Tolo
People from Civil aviation arrived around 5 to tell me and I was very angry because I told them you knew about this.

Commentary six
What for the CAA was a PR disaster and for some in the media a case of pilot error, was for the families something far more sinister. They claimed that both the pilot and first officer had voiced concerns about safety and maintenance at the CAA, the very organisation responsible for ensuring our safety in the air.

Jacob Lekalakala
She was worried. She was saying that, you know, I come from the Air Force, and what I know is that normally the engineers will come in and they will check And before you leave, they also check it. Then they sign the book. But here, nothing is happening.

BONGANI LINK
Jacob Lekalakala allowed himself time to grieve his wife Tebogo’s death, but then he wanted justice -and he began to dig for information. Now as a licensed aircraft maintenance engineer he was perfectly placed to find answers.

Jacob
I owed it to the aviation industry to expose the truth.

Commentary seven
A trail of his wife’s emails revealed several of her colleagues were concerned about the plane, too.

Jacob
It was concerns from the flying crew. Together with the inspectors. I realized, hey, look, I'm on the right track here. Keep on digging, keep on digging.

BONGANI LINK
But it wasn’t just the pilots that had had their concerns about the CAA’s aircraft. Warnings had come from inside the Civil Aviation Authority itself– the man at the very head of the Accident and incident investigation Division

Commentary eight
Peter Mashaba has been muzzled by the courts because his boss Poppy Khoza Director of the CAA, and the accountable officer of the flight inspection unit accused him of defamation and spreading confidential information about the CAA




Bongani
Part of why the CAA has a problem with you were discussing confidential information on WhatsApp groups?

Peter Mashaba
I still believe that I did not disclose any confidential information and the court will make a determination on that.

Commentary nine
While still at the CAA, it had been Mashaba who’d roped in the Ethiopian Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau to conduct the independent investigation the families of the deceased had demanded.

Fikile Mbalula up sound
On Sunday 23rd I met the families and handed over the final report...

Earlier this week, Transport Minister, Fikile Mbalula, released their final report.

Peter
The final report from Ethiopians -It stated that the director of civil aviation at the time of this fatal accident, is also held a position of an accountable manager for this flight inspection unit. Now the word speaks volumes. You are an accountable manager.

Commentary Ten
The report found 9 contraventions of the CAA’s own regulations. Also its certificate of airworthiness was rendered invalid by one of these contraventions

Bongani Is there any room in your mind that this could have been pilot error?
Peter Mashaba If I if I look at the findings, I find it very difficult to see this as a pilot error

Commentary eleven
The document includes this alarming detail: There was no cockpit voice recorder and the flight data recorder was non-compliant

Peter
The only two units that we rely on to extract information in order to find a conclusion is the cockpit voice recorder and the flight data recorder. Now we have been robbed information as aviators to establish what actually caused the loss of altitude by the crew, it could have been many things.

Commentary twelve
But ZS CAR had been investigated by Mashaba only two months before the fatal crash. In November 2019 its cockpit filled with smoke. Because both his report and the Ethiopian report are in the public domain, he is not bound by the gagging order


BONGANI
So when the aircraft crashed, you weren't surprised?
Peter Mashaba
Bongani looking at what we uncovered. And with this serious incident that happened two months before the crash, as an aviator and the former head of accident investigation, I look at this, it presents a picture of this was an accident waiting to happen!

Commentary thirteen
It’s an assessment unlikely to surprise Captain Tolo’s wife, Simnikitiwe, who was well aware of the aircraft’s troubled past.

Simnikiwe Tolo
He was in Lubumbashi where he landed this aircraft it had an engine problem, he came home pale he said this is going to kill me and then the other incident in 2019 the smoke in the cockpit. I have the WhatsApp where he said I was like a headless chicken after I landed I ran. Like he was not in his good mind, the way he was so shocked.

Commentary fourteen
The aircraft was released back into service on the 17th January 2020 after it had been grounded since November 2019. Six days later it crashed

Frans Modiroa
They feel that they are the authority, they have the power and are accountable to no one and when that happens, that's when you start to invite accidents to come in.

Commentary fifteen
Frans Modiroa is an aerospace consultant, and previously a board member of the International Air Service Council reporting directly to the Department of Transport. They, too, had concerns about the CAA and, specifically the flight inspection unit. But their attempts to raise the issue were ignored.

Frans
When you believe that you are high and mighty, you are untouchable. Things will happen.

Commentary sixteen
Like Jacob, Simnikitiwe and Mashaba, he believes the accident could have been avoided.

Frans Having been in industry for many years and a lot of people will tell you that there are signs that start talking to you -when you start missing those steps, they are talking to you- and from the way the aircraft performs, when you start having a number of technical snags building onto the aircraft and you not really getting to a point where you say, You know what? I think I have a potential flying coffin here.

Bongani to Mashaba
So here you are with a report, an independent report that pretty much aligns with what you said. And yet you've still got a court matter with the CAA and you taking them to the CCMA?


Peter Mashaba Absolutely. And Bongani, this final report, it's a very critical document. It's got serious implications on the country in the sense that many African states- they have a high regard of South African standards. Now, if one look at the findings of the final report it's now going to cause doubt in the South African aviation system.

Commentary seventeen
And that is doubly true if perhaps the most significant claim to emerge from this tragedy is true

Sims
That Saturday before the accident they were bombarding him with phone calls to come and fly this aircraft and he told me I am not going to go there Sim, because there is this part they cannot fix. The following day he went to a flight test and he said I am still not fine with this aircraft

Commentary eighteen
But he was assured the plane was fine and they took off the following day.

BONGANI LINK
It now appears that pressure may have been all about the money, because the Flight inspection unit of the CAA was generating good revenue for the CAA. But the plane had been on the ground for almost two months and so now there was a backlog to catch up.

Commentary nineteen
Time on the ground means money wasted. Airports across the country – and other parts of the region – pay the CAA to conduct calibration flights similar to the one attempted in George on that fateful morning.

Frans
I understand that the aircraft was obviously making money for South African civil aviation.
Bongani
Are you saying that compliance and safety measures might have been sacrificed here so that the CAA would be within its targets financial targets?
Frans
Yeah. The question has to be asked as to what really put them under so much pressure to operate an aircraft that had an outstanding issue with the International Air Service Council. It had a litany of technical problems.

Commentary twenty
In a letter to Carte Blanche the CAA says it’s not aware of any instances where the crew were put under pressure for the sake of profits or schedule, and that the FIU is not expected to yield any profits or revenue for the SACAA.


Bongani
Quite clearly. All is not well at the CAA?
Frans
I think South African Civil Aviation needs a total overall. And what's sad about it is whilst we're not getting everything in terms of what happened after this plane crash, some individuals are still there. So we don't know how much coverup is going on. We don't know what else they're doing.

BONGANI LINK
Then on Wednesday evening the CAA released a press statement. They are unhappy with the Ethiopians final report – they want the accident investigation reopened and they say they have contradictory evidence. This fight is far from over.

Commentary twenty-one
The CAA says that the final report contained new information that they were not given the opportunity to refute. Meanwhile the families are desperate for answers and closure

Jacob Lekalakala
Captain Tolo and Nguni and my wife also, they won’t forgive me if I just leave it here.
we need to teach our government that some sectors they might get away with it. Not in aviation, because aviation you make one mistake- people die.

THE END DURATION 12 31

PROMOS

PROMO ONE 11 seconds
This week a final report on an aircraft accident that killed three CAA flight crew, was released. It doesn’t look for the CAA that says they have contradictory evidence

PROMO TWO 21 seconds
The very organisation responsible for ensuring our safety in the air was flagged for violating its own regulations in an air Accident report, released this week

Jacob
I owed it to the aviation industry to expose the truth
Bongani
Quite clearly. All is not well at the CAA?
Frans
The South African Civil Aviation needs a total overall.





PROMO THREE 21 seconds
Families claim that the CAA plane in which their loved ones died in 2020, had a history of technical problems

Simnikiwe
People from Civil aviation arrived around 5 to tell me and I was very angry because I told them you knew about this.

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): A legal battle has broken out between the Director of our civil aviation authority Poppy Khoza and her former head of the accident and incident investigation division Peter Mashaba. Does an accident i
metadata.Unique Selling Point: AN EXCLUSIVE INTERVIEW WITH PETER MASHABA - former executive responsible for the Accident and Incident investigation division at the CAA
metadata.Summary: Khoza says he breached CAA confidentiality, insulted and defamed her. He says that she was warned that the CAA’s own plane would crash – she ignored the warnings and indeed a month later the CAA citation jet crashed in George and killed all three of its own crew. Khoza never renewed Mashaba’s contract and wanted an apology from him. He refused. The CAA and Khoza then went to court to gag Mashaba from any further utterances. Incredibly although this was about airline safety in South Africa and it called into question the regulatory authority’s own safety protocols, the matter was heard in camera. Carte Blanche tried to gain access to the courts and wrote a letter to the judge but we were rebuffed. The end result was that an interim interdict gagged Mashaba from speaking out and the CAA continued and Mashaba struggled on. But as with any investigation an independent body must do an accident investigation and make the final report public. In this case it was the Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau (AAIB) of Ethiopian Airlines. Tomorrow the report will be released by the DOT. And its findings says Mashaba vindicate what he was saying all along. Now he is fighting for his job back.
metadata.Further information: The findings suggest numerous breaches of safety by the CAA itself. And the allegations of an attempted cover up by the CAA is doing the rounds on pilot and aviation groups. Carte Blanche speaks to the main role players and investigates if the CAA tried to cover up, and put pressure on the Ethiopian Bureau to change the findings.
